note: WHY THE 1911 SHEETS' 'PRAIRIE AV. BLVD.' IS NOT A 1904 FACT. On 28 May 1904 the Council consented to the South Park Commissioners taking Prairie Avenue from 16th to 23rd Street, 16th Street from Michigan to Prairie, 23rd Street and South Park Avenue as a connecting boulevard (pp. 395-396). A consent is not a taking: the Commissioners' own compilation (south_park_commissioners_statutes_1908) records the effective consent as the city ordinance of 30 October 1905 and the Commissioners' selection and taking as 24 October 1906. On 1 July 1904 the avenue was a city street, paved and repaired by the city's Board of Local Improvements and Department of Public Works, which is what the city's own 1903, 1904 and 1906 records of it show.
what_it_supplies: that on 1 July 1904 the city had consented, five weeks earlier, to Prairie Avenue 16th-23rd and 16th Street becoming a South Park boulevard, and that the Commissioners had not yet taken them
